newsitem.title: USA: Ameritech disagrees with Justice Dept over phones.
newsitem.headline: Ameritech disagrees with Justice Dept over phones.

text.p: Ameritech Corp said Wednesday it disagreed with some of the "hurdles imposed" by the U.S. Justice Department in its evaluation of the company's application to provide long distance phone service in Michigan.
Robert Cooper, the president of Ameritech Michigan, said in a statement that those hurdles were "inconsistent with Congress' desire to jump-start competition in all communications markets."
The Justice Department urged phone regulators to reject Ameritech's bid to offer long distance service in Michigan, saying the Baby Bell had yet to fully open its local phone monopoly to competition.

The department noted that Ameritech has made "important progress" in opening its local phone network in that state, but said it had yet to go far enough to satisfy requirements outlined in last year's telecommunications law.

In particular, the Justice Department cited two items on a 14-point checklist in the law: one allowing competitors to direct the routing of calls, and another relating to the local transport system for carrying local calls.

"We'll continue to work with the Department of Justice, the Michigan Public Service Commission and Federal Communications Commission to achieve the intent of the Telecom Act and to bring the benefits of competition to consumers," Cooper said.
